summary: Intermittent 429s during ephemeral-key fan-out for large embedding job (KiteData, dedicated)
description: Issue summary: Customer KiteData reported bursts of 429s while executing a large fan-out embedding job. Impact: ~15% of embedding requests returned 429 over a 30-minute window, causing downstream job failures and retries. Environment: Dedicated pool (dk-01), prod-us-east, customer-configured client using per-job short-lived API keys (TTL ~5m). Observed behavior: Throttling occurs shortly after a coordinated client rollout that spun up ~250 ephemeral workers, each using a unique short-lived key. Expected behavior: Per-key burst limits should allow short warm-ups without triggering tenant-level throttling; overall tenant quotas should reflect sustained throughput rather than transient fan-outs. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and fix rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated-tenant account and obtain ability to mint short-lived keys (TTL 5 minutes).
2) Start 250 concurrent workers across multiple hosts; each worker mints a new short-lived key and immediately issues embedding batch requests (batch size 64).
3) Observe rate-limiter metrics and client responses over the next 10-30 minutes.
4) Repeat with longer lived keys (TTL > 1h) to compare behavior.

investigation_notes: Collected rate-limiter metrics and audit logs for tenant kitedata_tenant between 2026-03-10T13:50 and 2026-03-10T15:00.

Observed pattern: many short-lived key creations followed by immediate high-throughput requests. Per-key token buckets were initialized with warm-up tokens; warm-up charges were credited to tenant bucket due to a legacy aggregation path in api-gateway (keys without persisted mapping were attributed to tenant global counter).
Heatmap of request arrival time showed near-simultaneous start across workers -> amplified transient demand (burst amplification).
Replication in staging: reproduced 429s by emulating 200 short-lived keys with TTL 300s and same request pattern. Confirms gateway aggregation bug under concurrent ephemeral key churn.
Alternative hypotheses considered: noisy neighbor in Dedicated pool, autoscaling misfire, and model-side slowdown; telemetry did not show GPU contention or model queue backpressure.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: updated tenant routing config to treat newly minted short-lived keys as isolated per-key buckets for first 60s (prevent warm-up charge to tenant aggregate). Deployed to KiteData's gateway instance at 2026-03-10T18:12 and observed immediate drop in 429s.

Permanent fix: patched api-gateway to persist short-lived-key -> client mapping on creation and avoid fallback attribution to tenant bucket. Patch landed in github.com/redwood/infra/pull/7891 and rolled to prod-us-east on 2026-03-12 with canary and full roll-out.

Customer guidance: recommended best practices for high fan-out jobs: reuse keys for worker pools when possible, stagger key mint times during scale-up, implement exponential backoff with jitter and token-aware batching. SDKs were updated with a new helper to mint pooled keys and a sample backoff implementation.

Follow-ups: create an internal alerting rule for sudden short-lived-key churn per tenant (INT-8842), add a section to the public docs explaining short-lived-key interactions with rate-limits, and update Dedicated onboarding checklist to call out ephemeral-key patterns.
Status: Resolved for KiteData. Monitoring remains in place; no other tenants have shown the same pattern in the following 48 hours of telemetry.
